sections.section_title: Clinical Context and Pathophysiology of Exaggerated Growth
sections.description: This section establishes the foundational understanding of uterine leiomyomas during pregnancy, focusing on why they tend to grow larger, the specific risks posed to a nulliparous patient in her 40s, and how obesity can complicate physical assessment. It sets the stage for why these masses become clinically significant in the second trimester.
subtopics: Natural history of leiomyomas: Growth trends in the second and third trimesters due to hormonal influences (estrogen/progesterone).
Risk stratification for patients over 35 and the implications of advanced maternal age.
Impact of high BMI on clinical abdominal examination and palpation accuracy.
Mechanisms of mechanical compression causing dyspnea and abdominal pain in large mass scenarios.
Baseline obstetric considerations for a nulliparous patient at 21 weeks gestation.

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Evaluation: Imaging and Laboratory Interpretation
sections.description: This section details the modern diagnostic toolkit available during pregnancy, emphasizing safety profiles for the fetus. It teaches how to synthesize Ultrasound and MRI findings to differentiate between endometriomas and leiomyomas, and interprets the nuance of elevated CA-125 levels in this specific population.
subtopics: Initial Ultrasound findings: Challenges in differentiating cystic vs. solid lesions and assessing vascularity (Doppler).
Safety and efficacy of non-contrast MRI: Expectations from T1/T2 imaging and fetal exposure.
The diagnostic role of tumor markers (CA-125): Why elevated levels do not imply malignancy in the second trimester.
Interpretation of complex masses: Differentiating decidualized endometriomas from pedunculated myomas with cystic degeneration.
Integrating physical exam findings with imaging data to localize the anatomical origin of the masses.

sections.description: This section explores the critical pivot point in obstetric surgery: the decision to operate versus expectant management. It covers the multidisciplinary assessment required to balance the risk of acute maternal complications (torsion, rupture) against the risk of preterm labor and uterine entry points.
subtopics: Indications for surgical intervention: Symptomatic severity, organ compromise, and suspicion of malignant transformation.
Evaluating torsion risk in pedunculated masses: When mechanical twisting requires immediate excision.
Timing of surgery: Weathering the second trimester window vs. waiting until postpartum.
The Multidisciplinary Team approach: Coordination between Gynecologists, Obstetricians, and Surgeons.
Informed consent processes: Discussing risks of hysterectomy, preterm birth, and fetal loss with the patient.

sections.section_title: Surgical Technique and Intraoperative Obstetric Safety
sections.description: This section provides a technical overview of the surgical approach used for large abdominal masses within the gravid uterus. It covers the transition from diagnostic laparoscopy to laparotomy, techniques for ligating pedicles, methods for uterine repair, and specific protocols for fetal monitoring during the procedure.
subtopics: Surgical approach selection (Laparotomy vs. Laparoscopy) for massive 2nd-trimester masses.
Specific technique for resecting pedunculated leiomyomas: Clamping, twisting, and vascular control.
Decision to remove vs. leave masses in situ: Minimizing uterine fibrosis to protect future fertility and dilation.
Intraoperative Fetal Monitoring: Safety protocols to guarantee fetal heart rate stability during surgery.
Hemostatic techniques: Managing vascularity in myomas without inducing excessive bleeding or hypotension.

sections.section_title: Perinatal Outcomes, Delivery Planning, and Long-Term Resolution
sections.description: This section concludes the case trajectory by addressing the birthing plan dictated by the residual anatomical structures. It explains why an elective C-section was necessary despite the laparotomy, and discusses the natural regression of myomas postpartum and breastfeeding considerations.
subtopics: Delivery Mode: Why vaginal delivery is contraindicated with large posterior myomas near the contractile ring.
Timing of Elective C-Section: Balancing fetal lung maturity with myoma stabilization at 37 weeks.
Postoperative maternal recovery: Management of anemia, infection prophylaxis, and wound healing.
Long-term prognosis of uterine leiomyomas: Spontaneous regression in the postpartum period.
Decision-making regarding future surgical intervention: When to wait post-delivery for myoma reduction.
